activity.hint: Tells the hub whether each program on the watch list is running, so the PC device in SmartThings shows it on its "Watch list" card and routines can use it as a condition (Watch 1–5: running/stopped). Only the listed programs' file names, your labels and whether they run are sent; the names of programs not on the list are never sent anywhere. Off by default.

st.invite.steps:
How to install
1. Open the channel invite, tap [Enroll] and pick your hub
2. [Install] the SmartThings PC Control driver from the channel
3. In the SmartThings app, add the device with [+] → Add device → Scan nearby
4. Enter the secret (set on the Settings tab) in the new device's settings

svc.location.acl.body:
Current executable location:
%s

Users without admin rights can modify this folder. The service runs the executable and reads config.json from here as SYSTEM, so installing restricts the folder to administrators (other users can only read and run). Other files kept here, such as preset scripts, will need admin rights to change afterwards.

Recommended: keep only the executable in a dedicated folder such as %s.
svc.location.body:
Current executable location:
%s

The service points at the executable in this path, and config.json and service.log are created in the same folder. Downloads, Desktop, Documents and temp folders tend to get cleaned up or moved, and moving the file after installation breaks the service.

Recommended: move the executable to a permanent folder such as %s first, then install.
svc.location.shared.body:
Current executable location:
%s

Users without admin rights can modify this folder, and because it is shared with other files (a drive root, for example) its permissions are not locked down automatically. The service runs the executable from here as SYSTEM, so installing here lets other users replace it and take over the PC.

Recommended: move the executable to a dedicated folder such as %s first, then install.
svc.location.title: Check Install Location
svc.state.running.unreachable: The service is running but the app cannot connect. Another program may be using port %d — check service.log in the Logs tab.
